title: Ratecard-aware ingress normalizer for multi-provider metering
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We ingest usage events from multiple routing layers and external providers. Each source reports units differently (provider A = tokens, provider B = prompt/response pairs, provider C = embedding units). The downstream billing pipeline expects a canonical costable unit that maps to the customer ratecard for accurate invoices and real-time quota enforcement. Current ingestion presumes a single normalization path and fails for mixed-provider requests, leading to short-lived undercharging and later retroactive credits when reconciles run.
goal: Implement an ingress normalizer service that annotates, normalizes, and ratecard-maps incoming usage events into a single canonical token-cost tuple at ingest time. This reduces downstream backfills, enables immediate quota checks against reserved capacity, and surfaces per-route pricing mismatch metrics.
approach: 1) Deploy a stateless Ratecard Normalizer sidecar in the ingestion tier that attaches a normalized_cost_unit and lineage tags to each event. 2) Use a lightweight local cache of the effective ratecard (TTL 1m) keyed by customer_id+route to avoid synchronous reads to pricing store on hot paths. 3) Emit an ambiguity flag when rounding/estimation occurs (e.g., provider rounding, unknown model family). 4) Persist both raw_event and normalized_record to the ingest topic to allow downstream reconciler to rehydrated decisions if ratecards change.
tradeoffs:
- Eager normalization reduces downstream compute but increases coupling between price model changes and historical events (we persist normalization metadata per event to support re-evaluation).
- Cache improves latency but risks short-lived stale pricing; to mitigate we include cache-miss and cache-stale metrics and conservative TTL.
- Ambiguity flag will increase volume of reconciliation work for a small fraction of events; acceptable given customer impact reduction on the majority.
observability: Track metric: normalized_events_per_minute, normalization_latency_p50/p95, ratecard_cache_hit_ratio, events_marked_ambiguous, re-eval_reconciliations_triggered. Add dashboard in Console -> Billing -> Ingest Normalization. Create alert when ambiguity_rate > 0.5% or normalization_p95 > 150ms.
dataflow: ingest-proxy -> ratecard-normalizer-sidecar -> kafka.topic.normalized-ingest (raw + normalized) -> downstream metering-aggregator -> billing-attribution. The reconciler reads normalized records and uses canonical units for cost aggregation.
storage_and_retention: Normalized records stored in kafka for 30 days and in cold S3 for 3 years (for audit and regulatory queries). Keep raw_event for 90 days to allow forensic re-runs without full cold-store hit.
acceptance_criteria: Normalized events include canonical_unit, unit_count, cost_estimate_cents, ratecard_version, and ambiguity_flag
p95 normalization latency < 150ms end-to-end on our ingest instances at 95th percentile load
Ratecard cache hit ratio > 99% under typical traffic for customers with stable price plans
No regression in end-to-end billing totals > 0.5% compared to baseline for the test cohort during canary
Dashboard with metrics and an on-call runbook exists and is linked in the ticket
rollout_plan: 1) Implement and unit test normalizer. 2) Canary on 2% of traffic for 48 hours with synthetic tests to validate cost parity. 3) Expand to 25% for 4 days, run reconciliation job comparing old vs new pipeline. 4) Full rollout after sign-off from Billing PM and SRE. 5) Run one-week retroactive reconcile to surface any edge cases.
backfill_strategy: When ratecard changes require re-evaluation, run a targeted re-eval job on S3 cold store. Use the ambiguity_flag to prioritize re-runs. Provide a dry-run mode producing delta reports before applying credits.
security_and_privacy: No new PII stored in normalizer. Ratecard cache is in-memory only; metrics scrub customer IDs. Audit logs will reference event ids only. Security review: N/A for this iteration (config read-only), but revisit if we persist secrets.
open_risks: Edge cases where provider reports batched tokens differently (e.g., concatenated requests) — may under-approximate tokens
Large customers with frequent ratecard updates may cause cache churn and slightly higher normalization latency
Ambiguity volume spikes could pressure reconciliation workers
tests: Unit tests for mapping rules and rounding behavior
Integration test with pricing-store mock and kafka test harness
Load test to validate p95 latency and cache behavior at 10k rps
End-to-end reconciliation test comparing legacy vs normalized pipeline on historical window
